source_text: Φασὶν οἱ χείρονα λέγοντες οὐκ εἶναι τῆς σαρκὸς ἀνάστασιν. Ἀδύνατον γὰρ εἶναι τὴν φθειρομένην καὶ διαλυομένην ταύτην συναχθῆναι εἰς τὸ αὐτό. Πρὸς δὲ τὸ ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀσύμφορόν φασιν ὑπάρχειν τὴν ταύτης σωτηρίαν, καὶ κακίζουσιν αὐτὴν τὰ ἐλαττώματα προφέροντες, καὶ αὐτὴν μόνην τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων αἰτίαν ἀποφαίνονται, ὥστε, εἰ μέλλει, φασί, σὰρξ ἀνίστασθαι, καὶ τὰ ἐλαττώματα συναναστήσεται. Καὶ σοφίσματα πλέκουσι τοιαῦτα· Eἰ ἡ σὰρξ ἀνίσταται, ἤτοι ὁλόκληρος ἀναστήσεται καὶ πάντα τὰ μόρια ἔχουσα ἢ ἀτελής. Ἀλλὰ τὸ μὲν ἐλλειπῆ μέλλειν αὐτὴν ἀνίστασθαι ἀδυναμίαν ἐμφαίνει τοῦ ἀνιστῶντος, εἰ τὰ μὲν ἠδυνήθη σῶσαι, τὰ δὲ οὔ. Eἰ δὲ πάντα τὰ μέρη καὶ τὰ μόρια ἕξει, δῆλον ὅτι ταῦτα λέγειν ὑπάρχειν μετὰ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν πῶς οὐκ ἄτοπον, τοῦ σωτῆρος εἰρηκότος· Oὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίσκονται, ἀλλ' ἔσονται ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ; Oἱ δὲ ἄγγελοι, φασίν, οὔτε σάρκα ἔχουσιν οὔτε ἐσθίουσιν οὔτε συνουσιάζουσιν· ὥστε οὐδὲ σαρκικὴ ἀνάστασις γενήσεται. Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν καὶ τὰ τούτοις ὅμοια λέγοντες πειρῶνται διαστρέφειν τοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως. Eἰσὶ δέ τινες οἳ λέγουσι καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν Ἰησοῦν πνευματικὸν μόνον παρεῖναι, μηκέτι ἐν σαρκί, φαντασίαν δὲ σαρκὸς παρεσχηκέναι, πειρώμενοι καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀποστερεῖν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τὴν σάρκα. Πρῶτον μὲν τὰ ὑπ' αὐτῶν δοκοῦντα ἄπορα φαίνεσθαι λύσομεν· εἶθ' οὕτως ἑξῆς ἐπάξομεν τὸν ἀποδεικνύντα λόγον περὶ τῆς σαρκὸς ὡς ἔχει σωτηρίαν.
pass_a_gloss: They say, the ones speaking worse, that there is not a resurrection of the flesh. For it is impossible for this perishable and dissolvable flesh to be gathered again into the same. And they say that the salvation of it is impossible and unprofitable, and they blame it, bringing forth its weaknesses, and they declare it alone to be the cause of sins, so that, if the flesh is going to rise, they say, the weaknesses will also rise with it. And they weave such sophistries: If the flesh rises, either it will rise whole and having all its parts or incomplete. But that it is going to rise incomplete shows the weakness of the one rising it, if he was able to save some things but not others. And if it has all its parts and members, it is clear that to say these things exist after the resurrection from the dead is not absurd, since the Savior said: Neither do they marry nor are given in marriage, but they will be like angels in heaven? And the angels, they say, have neither flesh nor do they eat nor do they cohabitate; so neither will there be a fleshly resurrection. Saying these things and things similar to them, they try to pervert those from the faith. There are also some who say that Jesus himself is only spiritual, no longer in flesh, and that he provided an illusion of flesh, trying also to deprive the flesh of the promise. First, we will solve the things that seem difficult to them; then thus we will bring forth the demonstrating word concerning the flesh, how it has salvation.

pass_b_english: Those who argue for the worse position deny that there is a resurrection of the flesh. For they claim it is impossible for this perishable, dissolvable flesh to be gathered back into the same state. They also assert that its salvation is both impossible and unprofitable. They malign it by parading its weaknesses, and they pronounce it the sole cause of sins, so that, they say, if the flesh is to rise, its weaknesses will rise along with it. They weave sophistries like these: If the flesh rises, either it will rise whole, possessing all its parts, or it will rise incomplete. But to say it will rise incomplete reveals the weakness of the one raising it, if he was able to save some parts but not others. And if it possesses all its parts and members, it is clear that affirming these things exist after the resurrection from the dead is not absurd, since the Savior said, "They neither marry nor are given in marriage, but will be like angels in heaven" (Matthew 22:30). The angels, they claim, have neither flesh, nor do they eat, nor do they cohabit; therefore, there will be no fleshly resurrection either. By saying these things and others like them, they attempt to lead astray those who hold the faith. There are also some who say that Jesus himself is present only in a spiritual manner, no longer in flesh, and that he provided only an illusion of flesh, trying thereby to deprive the flesh of the promise as well. First, we will resolve the difficulties they imagine; then we will proceed to present the argument that demonstrates how the flesh possesses salvation.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required scripture citation (Matthew 22:30) for the quote 'Neither do they marry nor are given in marriage, but they will be like angels in heaven' which was present in the Greek but lacked a citation in the source text.
